decision_groups.reason: Literal checked-in help examples target exactly the same Azure SQL database/server/resource group. DB show is resource metadata, not table contents; direct managed-DB deletion belongs to CAT-3.4 rather than IaC.

LTR backup destruction is distinct from database deletion. Both commands select southeastasia/myserver/mydb; quoted semicolon in backup name remains part of one Bash argument, not a command separator. List inventories that exact backup container, without reading backup contents or implying it is the sole copy.

Managed Instance deletion has broader database scope than individual SQL DB deletion. Same mygroup/myinstance show is configuration/status metadata, not password retrieval; administrator login/endpoint may appear. Correct --yes description; no inferred approval or backups.
Managed individual DB in a SQL MI is a different API/resource scope from standalone SQL DB or whole MI. Same group/MI/DB show inspects database metadata without querying rows.
Cosmos account-wide data destruction vs metadata of the same account/resource group. show is not keys list or connection-strings listing; no key-retrieval example imported.

Legacy Core/SQL database deletion is actual registered source behavior at pinned revision: deprecated hidden group remains in commands.py, DeleteDatabase and ReadDatabase callbacks in custom.py. Latest rendered legacy URL returned404, so source-version qualification is mandatory. No invented conversion to modern syntax.

MongoDB API database deletion versus MongoDB DB resource inventory within same MyAccount/MyResourceGroup. Different API/data model from legacy Core DB and account-wide deletion, not a name substitution; list does not return documents.
MySQL Flexible Server database delete/show literals match testGroup/testserver/testDatabase; show describes database resource properties, not its SQL rows. test names are not proof of isolation.

Whole MySQL Flexible Server destruction differs materially from deleting one contained database. Same server/group inspection is a genuine metadata alternative. --yes does not imply permission; server backups are not assumed either absent or retained.

Actual whole-ADLS-filesystem delete/show source pair, distinct from baseline blob batching or Azure Files share deletion. Dummy 0000-0000 is preserved and explicitly qualified as an authentication gate; classification is static documented operation intent, not successful execution of invalid-looking credentials. No login rewrite, generated key or secret retained. Prefer other closed pairs for operationally less qualified exact-250 selection if desired; this is not an invented source or failure count.

Both actual examples use login authentication and same ADLS account/filesystem/directory. CLI dispatch/SDK source independently establishes recursive=True for deletion; exists is boolean. This recursive subtree scope differs from whole filesystem destruction.

Actual pinned MicrosoftDocs YAML examples and code grant support PostgreSQL Flexible Server DB delete/show with identical group/server/database. PostgreSQL managed API is a distinct database engine/utility family from MySQL, not a resource rename; no missing live _help.py source was fabricated.

DynamoDB on-demand USER backup deletion differs from baseline table deletion. Exact same backup ARN in both original RST command blocks; continuation ends at ARN and no Output JSON/prose is imported. Describe returns backup/table metadata, not items or credentials.

Actual Google Cloud SQL PostgreSQL guide contains database delete and same-instance database list. Both use unchanged active gcloud project/account selectors; no differing explicit project is introduced. Uppercase identifiers are literal source placeholders, not environment expansions or angle-bracket redirections.

Actual MySQL guides contain whole-instance delete and metadata describe with identical INSTANCE_NAME and explicit PROJECT_ID. Different scope from a contained database. Description/status/endpoint/certificate-public metadata are not database rows or client private-key retrieval; no --show-secrets, keys list or connection-string export occurs.
